name: Shoulder Pendulum
desc: Stand beside a sturdy table, support yourself with one hand, and lean forward so the other arm hangs loosely. Shift your body gently to let the relaxed arm swing forward and backward, side to side, or in small circles without actively lifting the shoulder.

name: Shoulder Flexion Table Slide
desc: Sit facing a table with your forearm resting on a towel and your thumb pointing upward. Slide the arm forward as you lean from your hips, then return to sitting upright while keeping the shoulder relaxed.

name: Wand-Assisted Shoulder External Rotation
desc: Lie on your back with your elbow bent and a small towel between your upper arm and your side, holding a stick in both hands. Use the opposite hand to guide the working forearm outward while keeping the elbow against the towel and avoiding a forced stretch.

name: Wand-Assisted Shoulder Abduction
desc: Stand upright with a stick held in both hands and the working hand near one end. Use the other arm to guide the working arm out to the side and upward within a comfortable range, then lower it without leaning or shrugging.

name: Active Shoulder Flexion
desc: Sit or stand upright with your arm at your side and your thumb pointing forward. Raise the arm in front of you within a comfortable range, then lower it slowly while keeping your ribs from lifting and your shoulder from shrugging.

name: Shoulder Scaption
desc: Stand with your arms at your sides and your thumbs pointing upward. Lift your arms diagonally forward, between straight ahead and directly sideways, then lower them with control while keeping your shoulders relaxed.

name: Resistance Band Shoulder Extension
desc: Stand facing a resistance band securely anchored in front of you, holding an end with your elbow straight. Pull your arm backward toward your hip, then return slowly without leaning forward or arching your back.

name: Resistance Band Shoulder External Rotation
desc: Stand sideways to a securely anchored band with the working arm farther from the anchor, your elbow bent, and a towel between your elbow and your side. Rotate your forearm outward against the band, then return slowly while keeping the elbow in place.

name: Resistance Band Shoulder Internal Rotation
desc: Stand sideways to a securely anchored band with the working arm nearer the anchor and your elbow bent at your side. Bring your forearm across your abdomen against the band, then return slowly without rotating your trunk.

name: Isometric Shoulder Flexion
desc: Stand facing a wall with your elbow bent and a folded towel between your fist and the wall. Gently press forward into the towel without moving your arm or leaning your body, then relax.

name: Isometric Shoulder Extension
desc: Stand with your back near a wall and your elbow bent at your side, placing a folded towel behind the elbow. Press the elbow backward into the towel without moving your shoulder or arching your back, then relax.

name: Isometric Shoulder Abduction
desc: Stand sideways beside a wall with your arm at your side and a folded towel between the outside of your upper arm and the wall. Press your upper arm gently outward into the towel without leaning or lifting the arm, then relax.

name: Isometric Shoulder External Rotation
desc: Sit or stand with your elbow bent at your side and place your opposite hand against the outside of the working wrist. Try to rotate the working forearm outward while the other hand prevents movement, then relax without shrugging.

name: Isometric Shoulder Internal Rotation
desc: Sit or stand with your elbow bent at your side and place your opposite hand against the inside of the working wrist. Try to rotate the forearm toward your abdomen while the other hand prevents movement, then relax while keeping the elbow still.

name: Scapular Retraction
desc: Sit or stand upright with your arms relaxed at your sides. Draw your shoulder blades gently toward each other, then release without arching your back or lifting your shoulders toward your ears.

name: Scapular Depression
desc: Sit upright with your arms resting by your sides. Gently draw your shoulder blades downward away from your ears, then relax while keeping your neck long and avoiding a forceful downward push.

name: Supine Serratus Punch
desc: Lie on your back with one arm pointing toward the ceiling and the elbow straight. Reach your hand upward by lifting the shoulder blade slightly from the surface, then lower the shoulder blade without bending the elbow or rolling your trunk.

name: Resistance Band Row
desc: Stand facing a resistance band securely anchored in front of you and hold the ends with your arms reaching forward. Pull your elbows backward beside your ribs, then return slowly while keeping your chest upright and your shoulders away from your ears.

name: Prone T Raise
desc: Lie face down with your forehead supported on a folded towel and your arms spread out to the sides with thumbs pointing upward. Lift your arms slightly by drawing your shoulder blades together, then lower them without lifting your head or arching your lower back.

name: Prone Y Raise
desc: Lie face down with your forehead supported and your arms reaching diagonally overhead in a Y shape, thumbs pointing upward. Lift the arms slightly from the surface, then lower them while keeping your neck relaxed and avoiding a shoulder shrug.

name: Prone W Raise
desc: Lie face down with your forehead supported, elbows bent, and upper arms angled away from your sides to form a W shape. Lift your elbows and hands slightly while drawing your shoulder blades together, then lower them without extending your neck or back.

name: Wall Push-Up Plus
desc: Stand facing a wall with your palms at shoulder height and your feet slightly behind you. Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, then straighten them and gently push your chest farther away by spreading your shoulder blades while keeping your body aligned.

name: Forearm Wall Slide
desc: Stand facing a wall with your forearms resting against it and your elbows below shoulder level. Slide your forearms upward within a comfortable range, then lower them while gently pressing into the wall and keeping your ribs from flaring.

name: Ball-on-Wall Shoulder Circles
desc: Stand facing a wall with your palm on a small ball and your arm comfortably below shoulder height. Apply gentle pressure and move the ball in small circles while keeping your elbow nearly straight and your trunk still.

name: Shoulder Shrug
desc: Sit or stand upright with your arms resting at your sides. Lift your shoulders straight toward your ears, then lower them with control without rolling them or moving your head forward.

name: Resistance Band D1 Shoulder Flexion
desc: Stand with a band securely anchored low on the working-arm side and hold it with that hand near your outer hip, palm facing backward. Draw the hand diagonally across your body toward the opposite shoulder as your palm turns toward you, then return without twisting your trunk.

name: Resistance Band D2 Shoulder Flexion
desc: Stand with a band securely anchored low on the opposite side and hold it with the working hand near your opposite hip. Lift the arm diagonally upward and outward as your thumb turns back, then return slowly while keeping your ribs and pelvis steady.

name: Wall Shoulder Taps
desc: Stand facing a wall with both palms at shoulder height and your feet far enough back to create a gentle lean. Shift your weight onto one arm and lift the other hand to touch the opposite shoulder, then replace it while keeping your body aligned.

name: Elbow Flexion and Extension
desc: Sit with your upper arm relaxed beside your body and your palm facing upward. Bend your elbow to bring your hand toward your shoulder, then straighten it within a comfortable range without moving the upper arm.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
desc: Sit or stand with a light dumbbell in your hand, palm facing forward, and your elbow at your side. Bend the elbow to lift the weight toward your shoulder, then lower it slowly without swinging your trunk or lifting your upper arm.

name: Resistance Band Triceps Extension
desc: Stand facing a band securely anchored above you, holding the end with your elbow bent and tucked beside your ribs. Straighten your elbow to press your hand downward, then return slowly while keeping your upper arm still.

name: Isometric Elbow Flexion
desc: Sit with your elbow bent and your palm facing upward, placing your opposite hand over the working forearm near the wrist. Try to bend the elbow while the opposite hand prevents movement, then relax without lifting your shoulder.

name: Isometric Elbow Extension
desc: Sit with your elbow bent and place your opposite hand beneath the working forearm near the wrist. Try to straighten the elbow while the other hand prevents movement, then relax while keeping the upper arm beside your body.

name: Forearm Pronation and Supination
desc: Sit with your elbow bent at your side and your wrist straight. Turn your forearm so your palm faces upward, then downward, keeping your upper arm still and avoiding movement through the shoulder.

name: Resisted Forearm Pronation
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and your hand beyond the table edge, holding a light hammer by its handle with the head extending toward your thumb. Start with your palm facing upward and turn your forearm until your thumb points up, lifting the hammer head, then return slowly while keeping your wrist straight and your upper arm still.

name: Resisted Forearm Supination
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and your hand beyond the table edge, holding a light hammer by its handle with the head extending toward your thumb. Start with your palm facing downward and turn your forearm until your thumb points up, lifting the hammer head, then return slowly while keeping your wrist straight and your upper arm still.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Flexion
desc: Sit with your forearm supported on a table, palm facing upward, and your hand just beyond the edge while holding a light dumbbell. Bend your wrist to lift the weight toward your forearm, then lower it slowly while keeping your forearm on the table.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Extension
desc: Sit with your forearm supported on a table, palm facing downward, and your hand just beyond the edge while holding a light dumbbell. Lift the back of your hand toward the ceiling, then lower it slowly without lifting your forearm.

name: Resistance Band Wrist Radial Deviation
desc: Sit with your forearm supported, your thumb pointing upward, and a band held in the working hand with its other end secured below it. Tilt your wrist toward the thumb against the band's pull, then return while keeping your forearm still.

name: Resistance Band Wrist Ulnar Deviation
desc: Sit with your forearm supported, your thumb pointing upward, and a band held in the working hand while the other hand holds its opposite end above it. Tilt your wrist toward the little-finger side against the band, then return without rotating your forearm.

name: Isometric Wrist Flexion
desc: Sit with your forearm supported, palm upward, and wrist straight, placing your opposite hand against the palm of the working hand. Try to bend the wrist toward your forearm while the other hand prevents movement, then relax.

name: Isometric Wrist Extension
desc: Sit with your forearm supported, palm downward, and wrist straight, placing your opposite hand over the back of the working hand. Try to lift the wrist while the other hand prevents movement, then relax without lifting your forearm.

name: Wrist Circles
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and your hand beyond the edge of a table. Move your wrist through small, comfortable circles in each direction while keeping your forearm still and avoiding a forced end position.

name: Dart-Thrower's Wrist Motion
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and your hand relaxed beyond the edge of a table. Move your wrist diagonally backward toward the thumb side, then forward toward the little-finger side, as if gently throwing a dart, without rotating your forearm.

name: Finger Tendon Glides
desc: Sit with your forearm supported, wrist straight, and fingers pointing upward. Move through a hook fist with only the middle and tip joints bent, a tabletop with only the knuckles bent, a straight fist with knuckles and middle joints bent, and a full fist with all finger joints bent. Return to straight fingers between shapes without forcing the joints.

name: Finger Tip-Joint Blocking (DIP)
desc: Sit with your hand supported and use the opposite hand to steady a finger just below its last joint. Bend and straighten only the fingertip joint while keeping the middle joint still and avoiding pressure directly over the moving joint.

name: Finger Middle-Joint Blocking (PIP)
desc: Sit with your hand supported and use the opposite hand to steady the base segment of one finger. Bend and straighten that finger's middle joint while keeping its knuckle still and allowing the fingertip to stay relaxed.

name: Finger Abduction and Adduction
desc: Rest your forearm and palm on a table with your fingers straight and relaxed. Spread your fingers apart, then bring them back together while keeping your wrist still and avoiding a forceful stretch.

name: Tabletop Finger Lifts
desc: Place your hand palm down on a table with your fingers comfortably straight. Lift one finger slightly from the table and lower it, keeping the palm and other fingers relaxed against the surface.

name: Thumb Opposition
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and your wrist straight. Touch the pad of your thumb to each fingertip in turn, opening your hand between touches and avoiding a forceful pinch.

name: Thumb Palmar Abduction
desc: Rest the little-finger side of your hand on a table with your thumb beside the index finger. Move the thumb away from the palm toward the ceiling, then return while keeping your wrist still.

name: Thumb Radial Abduction
desc: Rest your hand palm down on a table with your fingers relaxed. Slide your thumb sideways away from your index finger along the table, then return without lifting the palm or bending the wrist.

name: Thumb Knuckle Flexion (MCP)
desc: Sit with your hand supported and use the opposite hand to steady the thumb just below its knuckle. Bend the thumb at the knuckle while keeping its tip joint relaxed, then straighten it without moving the wrist.

name: Thumb Tip Joint Blocking
desc: Sit with your hand supported and use the opposite hand to steady the thumb below its tip joint. Bend and straighten the tip of the thumb while keeping the lower part of the thumb still.

name: Therapy Putty Grip
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and a ball of soft therapy putty in your palm. Curl your fingers around the putty and gently squeeze, then release while keeping your wrist straight and your thumb relaxed.

name: Therapy Putty Key Pinch
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and hold soft therapy putty between your thumb pad and the side of your index finger. Gently compress the putty as if holding a key, then release without bending your wrist.

name: Therapy Putty Tip Pinch
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and hold soft therapy putty between the tips of your thumb and index finger. Gently pinch the putty and release while keeping your wrist straight and avoiding collapse of the thumb joints.

name: Therapy Putty Tripod Pinch
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and hold soft therapy putty between your thumb, index finger, and middle finger. Press the three fingertips together into the putty, then release while keeping your wrist relaxed.

name: Resistance Band Finger Extension
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and a loose, light resistance loop around your fingertips and thumb. Open your fingers and thumb against the loop, then close them slowly while keeping your wrist straight and avoiding snapping the band.

name: Therapy Putty Finger Adduction
desc: Sit with your hand supported and place a small piece of soft therapy putty between two neighboring fingers. Gently squeeze the fingers together through the putty, then release while keeping them comfortably straight.

name: Cervical Rotation
desc: Sit upright with your shoulders relaxed and your chin level. Slowly turn your head to look over one shoulder, return to the center, and turn the other way without twisting your torso or forcing the range.

name: Cervical Flexion
desc: Sit upright with your shoulders relaxed. Slowly lower your chin toward your chest, then return to a level gaze without rounding your trunk or pulling on your head.

name: Cervical Extension
desc: Sit upright with your chin level and your shoulders relaxed. Gently look upward within a comfortable range, then return to the starting position without leaning backward through your trunk.

name: Cervical Side Bending
desc: Sit upright with your head centered over your shoulders. Gently bring one ear toward the same-side shoulder, return to center, and move to the other side without turning your head or lifting a shoulder.

name: Cervical Retraction
desc: Sit upright and look straight ahead with your shoulders relaxed. Slide your head straight backward to draw your chin inward, then release without looking down or tilting your head upward.

name: Supine Chin Nod
desc: Lie on your back with your head supported on a thin pillow or folded towel. Gently nod as if saying yes, drawing your chin slightly toward your throat, then release without lifting your head or pressing it firmly into the support.

name: Isometric Cervical Flexion
desc: Sit upright with your head centered and place your palm on your forehead. Gently press your forehead into your hand while preventing movement, then relax while breathing normally and keeping your shoulders relaxed.

name: Isometric Cervical Extension
desc: Sit upright with your head centered and place your hand against the back of your head. Gently press backward into your hand without tilting or moving your head, then relax without arching your back.

name: Isometric Cervical Side Bending
desc: Sit upright and place your hand against the side of your head above your ear. Gently try to tilt your head toward that side while your hand prevents movement, then relax while keeping your shoulders level.

name: Isometric Cervical Rotation
desc: Sit upright and place your palm against the side of your forehead near the temple. Gently try to turn your head toward that hand while preventing movement, then relax without tilting your head or turning your torso.

name: Quadruped Cervical Retraction
desc: Start on your hands and knees with your back level and your gaze toward the floor. Draw your chin inward to align your head with your spine, then relax slightly without letting your head drop or looking upward.

name: Supine Chin Tuck with Head Lift
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your head resting on the surface. Gently tuck your chin, lift your head just clear of the surface while keeping the tuck, then lower with control without jutting your chin forward.

name: Seated Thoracic Rotation
desc: Sit upright with your feet on the floor and your arms crossed over your chest. Turn your chest gently to one side, return to center, and turn the other way while keeping your pelvis facing forward.

name: Side-Lying Open Book
desc: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, your head supported, and your arms reaching forward with palms together. Open the top arm toward the other side as your chest rotates, then return while keeping your knees stacked and avoiding a forced reach to the floor.

name: Thread the Needle
desc: Start on your hands and knees with your hands beneath your shoulders. Slide one arm under the opposite arm as your upper body rotates toward the floor, then return while keeping your hips above your knees and moving within a comfortable range.

name: Seated Thoracic Extension over Chair
desc: Sit with your feet flat and the back of a sturdy chair contacting your mid-back below the shoulder blades. Support your head with your hands and gently extend your upper back over the chair, then return without forcing your neck backward or arching your lower back.

name: Seated Thoracic Flexion
desc: Sit upright with your feet flat and your hands resting on your thighs. Gently round your upper back as your shoulder blades move apart, then return upright while keeping your pelvis supported and avoiding a forceful neck bend.

name: Seated Thoracic Side Bending
desc: Sit upright with your feet flat and your hands resting lightly behind your head. Bend your upper body gently to one side, return upright, and move to the other side without rotating or lifting either hip from the chair.

name: Cat-Cow
desc: Start on your hands and knees with your hands beneath your shoulders and your knees beneath your hips. Gently round your back upward, then let it soften into a slight arch while moving your head with your spine and avoiding a forced end range.

name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
desc: Start on your hands and knees and place one hand lightly behind your head. Turn your chest to bring that elbow toward the opposite forearm, then open the elbow toward the ceiling while keeping your hips still and avoiding pressure on your neck.

name: Bench Thoracic Extension
desc: Kneel facing a stable bench with your elbows supported on it and your palms together. Move your hips backward and let your chest lower between your arms, then return while keeping your abdomen gently engaged to limit lower-back arching.

name: Prone Thoracic Extension
desc: Lie face down with your arms at your sides and a folded towel beneath your forehead. Gently lift your upper chest a small amount, then lower it while keeping your chin tucked, your pelvis grounded, and your lower back from arching excessively.

name: Abdominal Bracing
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat. Gently tighten your abdomen as if preparing for a light push, then relax while breathing normally and avoiding a forceful flattening of your back.

name: Posterior Pelvic Tilt
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat. Gently roll your pelvis to bring your lower back closer to the surface, then release while keeping your buttocks down and avoiding pushing through your feet.

name: Hooklying March
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat, and abdomen gently engaged. Lift one foot a small distance as if marching, lower it, and alternate sides without rocking your pelvis or holding your breath.

name: Bent-Knee Fallout
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat. Let one knee open slowly to the side and return while keeping your pelvis level and the opposite leg still.

name: Dead Bug
desc: Lie on your back with your arms pointing upward and your hips and knees bent so your shins are parallel to the floor. Slowly reach one arm overhead as the opposite leg extends, then return while keeping your lower back and pelvis steady within a range you can control.

name: Bird Dog
desc: Start on your hands and knees with your back level and your abdomen gently engaged. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg backward, then return without rotating your pelvis or lifting the leg above your trunk.

name: Quadruped Arm Lift
desc: Start on your hands and knees with your hands beneath your shoulders and your back level. Reach one arm forward and replace it, alternating sides while keeping your trunk still and your weight evenly supported through the remaining hand and knees.

name: Forearm Plank
desc: Lie face down and support yourself on your forearms with your elbows beneath your shoulders and your toes on the floor. Lift your body into a straight line from head to heels, then lower with control while breathing normally and avoiding a sagging lower back.

name: Side Plank from Knees
desc: Lie on your side with your knees bent and your elbow directly beneath your shoulder. Lift your hips to align your shoulders, hips, and knees, then lower with control while keeping your chest facing forward and breathing normally.

name: Abdominal Curl-Up
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your hands resting on your thighs. Gently tighten your abdomen and lift your head and shoulder blades slightly as your hands slide toward your knees, then lower without pulling your head forward or holding your breath.

name: Glute Bridge
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat, about hip-width apart. Press through your feet to lift your hips until your trunk and thighs align, then lower slowly without arching your back or letting your knees fall inward.

name: Single-Leg Bridge
desc: Lie on your back with one foot flat, the other leg lifted with its knee bent, and your arms resting by your sides. Push through the planted foot to lift your hips, then lower while keeping your pelvis level and avoiding a lower-back arch.

name: Pallof Press
desc: Stand sideways to a resistance band securely anchored at chest height and hold it with both hands against your chest. Press your hands straight forward, then bring them back while resisting the band's pull and keeping your chest and pelvis facing ahead.

name: Resistance Band Trunk Rotation
desc: Stand with your feet apart beside a band securely anchored at chest height and hold it with both hands in front of you. Turn your chest away from the anchor and return with control, allowing your feet to pivot so your knees and back are not forced to twist.

name: Resistance Band High-to-Low Chop
desc: Stand sideways to a band securely anchored above shoulder height and hold it with both hands near the anchor. Draw your hands diagonally downward toward the opposite hip, then return while turning through your hips and feet and keeping your back from rounding.

name: Resistance Band Low-to-High Lift
desc: Stand sideways to a band securely anchored near the floor and hold it with both hands near the anchor-side hip. Lift your hands diagonally toward the opposite shoulder, then return with control while allowing your feet to pivot and avoiding a backward lean.

name: Supine Tabletop Toe Taps
desc: Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent and your shins parallel to the floor. Lower one foot to lightly touch the floor and lift it back, alternating sides while keeping your knee bent and your pelvis steady.

name: Supine Hand-to-Thigh Isometric Press
desc: Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent and your hands resting against the fronts of your thighs. Gently press your hands into your thighs as your thighs press back without movement, then relax while keeping your back steady and breathing normally.

name: Quadruped Knee Hover
desc: Start on your hands and knees with your hands beneath your shoulders, knees beneath your hips, and toes tucked under. Gently tighten your abdomen and lift your knees just clear of the floor, then lower them while keeping your back level and breathing normally.

name: Suitcase Carry
desc: Stand upright holding a light weight in one hand at your side. Walk along a clear, level path while keeping your shoulders and pelvis level and avoiding leaning toward or away from the weight.

name: Seated Stability Ball Pelvic Circles
desc: Sit near the center of a stability ball with your feet wide enough for support and a sturdy surface within reach. Slowly move your pelvis in small circles while keeping your upper body relaxed and both feet planted, then reverse direction.

name: Seated Stability Ball March
desc: Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat and a sturdy support within reach. Lift one foot slightly and replace it, alternating sides while keeping the ball as still as possible and your trunk upright.

name: Supine Lower Trunk Rotation
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat, and arms resting out to the sides. Let both knees move gently toward one side, return to center, and move to the other side while keeping your shoulders on the surface.

name: Prone Press-Up
desc: Lie face down with your palms beneath your shoulders and your legs relaxed. Press through your hands to lift your upper body within a comfortable range, then lower while keeping your pelvis on the surface and avoiding a forced bend in your lower back.

name: Gluteal Isometric Squeeze
desc: Lie on your back with your legs comfortably supported. Gently tighten your buttock muscles together, then relax without lifting your hips, squeezing your thighs together, or holding your breath.

name: Supine Hip Abduction Slide
desc: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your toes pointing toward the ceiling. Slide one leg out to the side and back along the surface while keeping your knee straight and your pelvis still.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
desc: Lie on your side with your lower knee bent, your upper leg straight, and your hips stacked. Lift the upper leg slightly upward and lower it slowly while keeping your toes facing forward and avoiding rolling your pelvis backward.

name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction
desc: Lie on your side with your lower leg straight and your upper leg bent in front of you with its foot on the floor. Lift the lower leg toward the ceiling and lower it slowly while keeping your hips steady and your knee straight.

name: Prone Hip Extension
desc: Lie face down with your legs straight and your pelvis resting on the surface. Tighten one buttock and lift that leg slightly, then lower it without bending the knee, twisting your pelvis, or arching your lower back.

name: Resistance Band Hip Flexion
desc: Stand facing away from a band securely anchored low behind you, with the other end fastened around one ankle and a sturdy support within reach. Lift the working thigh forward against the band, allowing the knee to bend, then return without leaning backward.

name: Clamshell
desc: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, your feet together, and your hips stacked. Lift the upper knee while keeping your feet touching, then lower it without rolling your pelvis backward.

name: Reverse Clamshell
desc: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent and your knees resting together. Lift the upper foot away from the lower foot while keeping the knees in contact, then lower it without rotating your pelvis.

name: Prone Hip Internal and External Rotation
desc: Lie face down with one knee bent so the lower leg points upward. Move the foot gently outward and inward as your thigh rotates, then return to center while keeping your pelvis flat and the knee in place.

name: Hip Adduction Ball Squeeze
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and a soft ball or folded pillow between them. Gently squeeze inward against the object, then relax while keeping your feet planted and your pelvis still.

name: Standing Hip Abduction Wall Press
desc: Stand sideways beside a wall with the nearer hip and knee slightly bent and a folded towel between the outside of that knee and the wall. Press the knee outward into the wall without moving it, then relax while keeping your standing knee soft and your pelvis level.

name: Seated Hip Flexion Isometric
desc: Sit upright with your feet flat and place your hands on top of one thigh near the knee. Try to lift that thigh while your hands prevent movement, then relax without leaning backward or holding your breath.

name: Standing Hip Extension Isometric
desc: Stand facing away from a wall with one heel lightly contacting it and a sturdy support beside you. Gently press the heel backward into the wall without moving your leg, then relax while keeping your trunk upright and your pelvis facing forward.

name: Lateral Resistance Band Walk
desc: Stand with a resistance loop around your thighs just above your knees and your hips and knees slightly bent. Step sideways and bring the trailing foot toward the lead foot without letting the band go slack, keeping your toes forward and knees aligned over your feet.

name: Monster Walk
desc: Stand with a resistance loop around your thighs just above your knees and your feet apart in a shallow squat. Take diagonal steps forward and then backward while maintaining space between your knees and avoiding inward knee collapse.

name: Hip Hike
desc: Stand on one leg on a low, stable step with the other foot hanging over the edge and a railing within reach. Lower the unsupported side of your pelvis slightly, then lift it back to level while keeping your standing knee nearly straight and your trunk upright.

name: Lateral Lunge
desc: Stand with your feet facing forward and a sturdy support within reach. Step to one side and bend that hip and knee as you sit your hips backward, then push through that foot to return while keeping the other leg relatively straight.

name: Reverse Lunge
desc: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and a sturdy support within reach. Step one foot backward and bend both knees within a comfortable range, then push through the front foot to return while keeping the front knee aligned over the foot.

name: Split Squat
desc: Stand in a staggered stance with one foot forward and the other behind, using a sturdy support for balance. Bend both knees to lower your body and straighten them to rise while keeping your feet in place and your front knee aligned over the foot.

name: Seated 90/90 Hip Rotation Switch
desc: Sit on a mat with both knees bent and your feet wider than your hips, placing your hands behind you for support. Gently lower both knees toward one side, return through the center, and lower them toward the other side without forcing either knee to the floor.

name: Quadruped Hip Abduction
desc: Start on your hands and knees with your back level and your abdomen gently engaged. Lift one bent knee out to the side and return while keeping your pelvis facing the floor and avoiding leaning onto the opposite arm.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
desc: Stand on one leg with a soft knee and a sturdy support within reach. Hinge forward at the hip as the other leg reaches backward, then return upright while keeping your back long and your pelvis facing the floor.

name: Hip Hinge
desc: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your knees slightly bent. Move your hips backward as your trunk tips forward, then straighten through your hips while keeping your back long and your weight balanced over your feet.

name: Adductor Rockback
desc: Start on your hands and knees and extend one leg out to the side with its foot on the floor. Move your hips backward and return within a comfortable range while keeping your back long and the outstretched knee straight.

name: Quadriceps Set
desc: Lie on your back with one leg straight and a small folded towel beneath that knee. Tighten the front of your thigh to press the knee gently toward the towel, then relax without lifting your heel or holding your breath.

name: Short Arc Quadriceps Extension
desc: Lie on your back with a firm rolled towel or bolster beneath one knee so it starts slightly bent. Straighten the knee to lift your heel, then lower it slowly while keeping the back of the knee supported on the roll.

name: Seated Knee Extension
desc: Sit upright with your thighs supported and your feet clear enough to move freely. Straighten one knee to lift the foot, then lower it slowly while keeping your thigh on the seat and avoiding leaning backward.

name: Straight Leg Raise
desc: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the working leg straight. Tighten the front of the straight thigh and lift that leg to about the height of the opposite thigh, then lower it without bending the working knee or arching your back.

name: Heel Slide
desc: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your heel resting on the surface. Slide one heel toward your buttock to bend the knee, then slide it away again while keeping the foot aligned with the leg and avoiding a forced bend.

name: Seated Assisted Knee Flexion
desc: Sit on a sturdy chair with the working foot on the floor and the opposite foot in front of its ankle. Use the opposite foot to gently guide the working foot backward under the chair, then release while keeping your thigh supported and avoiding a forced bend.

name: Heel Prop Knee Extension
desc: Lie on your back with your heel supported on a firm rolled towel and your knee unsupported. Let the knee gradually relax toward a straighter position, then remove the support without pressing down on the knee or placing a weight over it.

name: Resistance Band Terminal Knee Extension
desc: Stand facing a band securely anchored in front of you at knee height, with the loop resting behind one knee and a support within reach. Start with that knee slightly bent, then straighten it against the band's pull and release without locking it backward or shifting your trunk.

name: Standing Hamstring Curl
desc: Stand upright beside a sturdy support with your knees close together. Bend one knee to bring your heel toward your buttock, then lower it slowly while keeping your thigh vertical and avoiding arching your back.

name: Hamstring Heel-Dig Isometric
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your heels on the surface. Press one heel downward as if trying to drag it toward you without allowing it to slide, then relax while keeping your pelvis down.

name: Wall Sit
desc: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet forward far enough to support a shallow squat. Slide downward within a comfortable range and maintain the position while breathing normally, then slide upward while keeping your knees aligned with your feet.

name: Mini Squat
desc: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a sturdy support within reach. Bend your hips and knees into a shallow squat, then straighten while keeping your heels down and your knees aligned over your feet.

name: Single-Leg Mini Squat
desc: Stand on one leg beside a sturdy support with the other foot lifted slightly. Bend the standing hip and knee into a shallow squat, then straighten while keeping your pelvis level and your knee aligned over your foot.

name: Forward Step-Up
desc: Stand facing a low, stable step with a railing or sturdy support beside you. Place one foot fully on the step and push through it to bring your body upward, then step back down with control while keeping the lead knee aligned over the foot.

name: Forward Step-Down
desc: Stand on a low, stable step with a railing within reach. Slowly bend the supporting knee to lower the opposite heel toward the floor in front of you, then straighten to return while keeping your pelvis level and avoiding inward knee movement.

name: Lateral Step-Down
desc: Stand sideways on a low, stable step with the working foot on the step and a railing within reach. Bend the working knee to lower the opposite heel toward the floor beside the step, then rise while keeping your hips level and your knee aligned over your foot.

name: Leg Press
desc: Sit in a leg press machine with your back supported and your feet comfortably apart on the platform, using a light resistance and the machine's safety settings. Push the platform away by straightening your hips and knees, then return slowly without locking your knees or letting your pelvis lift from the seat.

name: Stability Ball Hamstring Curl
desc: Lie on your back with your heels on a stability ball and your arms resting on the floor for support. Lift your hips slightly and bend your knees to roll the ball toward you, then roll it away while keeping your pelvis level and your movement controlled.

name: Seated Knee Extension Isometric
desc: Sit upright with your knee bent and use the opposite ankle to gently block the front of the working ankle. Try to straighten the working knee without allowing movement, then relax while keeping your thigh supported and breathing normally.

name: Lateral Step-Up
desc: Stand sideways beside a low, stable step with a railing or sturdy support within reach. Place the nearer foot fully on the step and push through it to rise, then lower with control while keeping your pelvis level and the working knee aligned over the foot.

name: Ankle Pumps
desc: Sit or lie with your leg supported and your foot free to move. Pull your foot toward your shin and point it away, alternating smoothly while keeping your knee still and avoiding forceful toe gripping.

name: Ankle Circles
desc: Sit with your lower leg supported and your foot free beyond the edge of the support. Move your ankle through small circles in each direction while keeping your knee still and avoiding a forced end range.

name: Active Ankle Inversion and Eversion
desc: Sit with your lower leg supported and your foot free to move. Turn the sole gently inward and outward while keeping your knee facing upward and moving through the ankle rather than rotating the whole leg.

name: Resistance Band Ankle Dorsiflexion
desc: Sit with your leg supported and a band around the top of your forefoot, securely anchored in front of you so it pulls your foot away from your shin. Pull your foot toward your shin, then return slowly while keeping your knee still and the band clear of your toes.

name: Resistance Band Ankle Plantar Flexion
desc: Sit with your leg supported and a band looped around the ball of your foot, holding the ends securely in your hands. Press the foot away from you against the band, then return slowly without curling your toes or moving your knee.

name: Resistance Band Ankle Inversion
desc: Sit with your leg supported and a band around your forefoot, securely anchored on the outer side of the working leg. Turn the sole inward against the band, then return slowly while keeping the knee still and avoiding rotation through your hip.

name: Resistance Band Ankle Eversion
desc: Sit with your leg supported and a band around your forefoot, securely anchored on the inner side of the working leg. Turn the sole outward against the band, then return slowly while keeping your knee steady and avoiding movement through your hip.

name: Isometric Ankle Dorsiflexion
desc: Sit with your leg supported and place your opposite hand over the top of the working forefoot. Try to pull the foot toward your shin while your hand prevents movement, then relax without gripping your toes.

name: Isometric Ankle Plantar Flexion
desc: Sit with your leg supported and place your opposite hand against the ball of the working foot. Try to point your foot away from you while your hand prevents movement, then relax while keeping your toes loose.

name: Isometric Ankle Inversion
desc: Sit with your lower leg supported and place your opposite hand against the inside edge of the working forefoot. Try to turn the sole inward while the hand prevents movement, then relax while keeping your knee still.

name: Isometric Ankle Eversion
desc: Sit with your lower leg supported and place your opposite hand against the outside edge of the working forefoot. Try to turn the sole outward while the hand prevents movement, then relax without rotating your whole leg.

name: Standing Bilateral Heel Raise
desc: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your hands lightly resting on a sturdy support. Rise onto the balls of both feet, then lower your heels slowly while keeping your ankles upright and your weight spread across the forefeet.

name: Single-Leg Heel Raise
desc: Stand on one foot beside a sturdy support with the other foot lifted. Rise onto the ball of the standing foot, then lower slowly while keeping your knee nearly straight and your ankle from rolling outward.

name: Seated Heel Raise
desc: Sit upright with your feet flat and your knees bent. Lift your heels while keeping the balls of your feet on the floor, then lower them slowly without rolling your ankles outward or gripping your toes.

name: Eccentric Heel Lowering
desc: Stand on a level floor beside a sturdy support and rise onto the balls of both feet. Shift your weight onto one foot, lift the other foot, and slowly lower the working heel to the floor before replacing the other foot.

name: Standing Toe Raise
desc: Stand with your back lightly supported against a wall and your feet slightly forward. Keep your heels on the floor as you lift the fronts of your feet, then lower them with control without leaning away from the wall.

name: Towel Toe Curls
desc: Sit with your heel planted and the front of your foot resting on a small towel. Curl your toes to draw the towel toward you, then release while keeping your heel down and avoiding movement through your knee.

name: Toe Spreading
desc: Sit with your foot resting flat on the floor and your ankle relaxed. Spread your toes apart, then relax them while keeping the ball of your foot grounded and avoiding curling the toes.

name: Toe Yoga
desc: Sit with your foot flat on the floor. Lift your big toe while keeping the smaller toes down, then lower it and lift the smaller toes while keeping the big toe down, using a hand to help isolate the movements if needed.

name: Short Foot Exercise
desc: Sit with your foot flat, your heel grounded, and your toes relaxed. Gently draw the ball of your foot toward your heel to raise the arch slightly, then release without curling your toes or rolling the ankle outward.

name: Assisted Great Toe Flexion and Extension
desc: Sit with your foot supported and use one hand to steady the forefoot near the big toe's base. Use the other hand to gently bend the big toe upward and downward within a comfortable range without twisting it or pulling on its tip.

name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Mobility
desc: Stand facing a wall with one foot close to it and the other behind for support. Bend the front knee toward the wall and return while keeping the front heel down and the knee moving in line with the middle toes.

name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
desc: Lie on your back with one knee bent and a strap around the sole of the other foot. Raise the strapped leg and gently straighten its knee until you feel a stretch behind the thigh, keeping your pelvis on the surface and avoiding a forceful pull.

name: Standing Quadriceps Stretch
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support and bend one knee to bring its heel toward your buttock. Hold the ankle with your hand or a strap and gently draw it closer until you feel a stretch at the front of the thigh, keeping your knees close and your back from arching.

name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
desc: Kneel on a padded surface with one foot in front and your back knee beneath your hip. Gently tuck your pelvis and shift forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip, keeping your trunk upright and avoiding a lower-back arch.

name: Standing Gastrocnemius Stretch
desc: Stand facing a wall with your hands supported, one foot forward, and the other behind with its knee straight. Shift toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf, keeping that heel down and its toes pointing forward.

name: Standing Soleus Stretch
desc: Stand facing a wall with your hands supported and one foot behind the other. Bend both knees and shift gently forward until you feel a stretch low in the back calf, keeping the rear heel down and the rear knee aligned with the foot.

name: Supine Figure-Four Piriformis Stretch
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and place one ankle across the opposite thigh above the knee. Hold behind the uncrossed thigh and gently draw it toward your chest until you feel a buttock stretch, keeping your head supported and avoiding pressure on the crossed knee.

name: Butterfly Adductor Stretch
desc: Sit upright with the soles of your feet together and your knees comfortably apart. Gently hinge forward from your hips until you feel a stretch along the inner thighs, keeping your back long and avoiding pushing down on your knees.

name: Standing Outer Hip Stretch
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support and cross the leg to be stretched behind the other leg. Shift your hips gently toward the crossed-leg side as your upper body leans away until you feel a stretch at the outer hip, keeping both feet supported and avoiding twisting.

name: Supine Gluteal Stretch
desc: Lie on your back with your head supported and one knee bent toward your chest. Hold behind that thigh and guide the knee slightly toward the opposite shoulder until you feel a buttock stretch, keeping the pelvis grounded and avoiding pulling directly on the knee joint.

name: Seated Plantar Fascia Stretch
desc: Sit with one ankle resting across the opposite thigh and steady the heel with one hand. Gently draw the toes upward with the other hand until you feel a stretch along the sole, keeping the ankle comfortable and avoiding a forceful pull.

name: Seated Toe Extensor Stretch
desc: Sit with your foot supported and use one hand to steady the front of the foot. Gently curl the toes downward with the other hand until you feel a light stretch across the top of the toes, keeping the ankle neutral and avoiding pressure on the toenails.

name: Seated Ankle Plantar Flexion Stretch
desc: Sit with your lower leg supported and your foot free to move. Use one hand to gently guide the whole foot downward until you feel a stretch across the front of the ankle, keeping the toes relaxed and avoiding twisting the foot inward.

name: Supine Hip Internal Rotation Stretch
desc: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet slightly wider than your hips. Let one knee drift gently inward while its foot stays planted, stopping at a comfortable hip stretch and keeping your pelvis level without pressing on the knee.

name: Child's Pose
desc: Start on your hands and knees on a padded surface with your knees comfortably apart. Move your hips toward your heels and reach your hands forward until you feel a gentle back stretch, then return without forcing your hips down or compressing your knees.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
desc: Sit or stand upright and bring one arm across your chest. Support that arm above the elbow with the opposite hand and gently draw it closer until you feel a stretch behind the shoulder, keeping the shoulder down and avoiding pressure directly on the elbow.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
desc: Stand in a doorway with your forearms resting on the frame and your elbows comfortably below shoulder height. Step forward slightly until you feel a stretch across your chest, keeping your ribs down and avoiding a forced reach behind your body.

name: Counter-Supported Latissimus Stretch
desc: Stand facing a sturdy counter with your hands resting on it and your elbows straight. Step back and hinge at your hips until you feel a stretch along the sides of your upper back, keeping your spine long and avoiding a forceful shoulder stretch.

name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
desc: Sit or stand upright and bend one elbow so your hand reaches toward your upper back. Use the other hand to gently support the raised upper arm until you feel a stretch behind it, keeping your neck relaxed and avoiding an arched back.

name: Standing Biceps Stretch
desc: Stand upright with your hands lightly clasped behind your hips and your palms facing your body. Gently straighten your elbows and move your hands slightly away until you feel a stretch at the fronts of your upper arms, keeping your shoulders relaxed and avoiding a forced lift.

name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
desc: Extend one arm in front of you with its palm facing upward and its elbow comfortably straight. Use the opposite hand to gently guide the fingers downward until you feel a stretch along the palm side of the forearm, keeping your shoulder relaxed and avoiding a forceful pull.

name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
desc: Extend one arm in front of you with its palm facing downward and its elbow comfortably straight. Use the opposite hand to gently bend the wrist so the fingers point toward the floor, stopping at a stretch along the back of the forearm without twisting the wrist.

name: Forearm Pronation Stretch
desc: Sit with your elbow bent at your side and your forearm supported. Use the opposite hand to gently guide the working forearm toward a palm-down position until you feel a mild stretch, keeping your elbow still and avoiding twisting through the shoulder.

name: Forearm Supination Stretch
desc: Sit with your elbow bent at your side and your forearm supported. Use the opposite hand to gently guide the working forearm toward a palm-up position until you feel a mild stretch, keeping your wrist straight and avoiding a forceful rotation.

name: Thumb Web-Space Stretch
desc: Sit with your forearm supported and your hand relaxed. Use the opposite hand to gently open the space between your thumb and index finger until you feel a light stretch, keeping the thumb joints slightly relaxed and avoiding pulling on the fingertip.

name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
desc: Sit upright and hold the chair beside you with the hand on the side to be stretched. Gently tilt your head toward the opposite shoulder until you feel a stretch along the side of your neck, keeping your chin facing forward and avoiding pulling on your head.

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
desc: Sit upright and hold the chair beside you with the hand on the side to be stretched. Turn your head slightly away from that side and look downward toward the opposite armpit until you feel a stretch behind the neck and shoulder, avoiding a forceful pull on your head.

name: Feet-Together Balance
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support with your feet together, knees slightly relaxed, and eyes looking forward. Maintain an upright position while breathing normally, using the support as needed and separating your feet to finish.

name: Semi-Tandem Balance
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support with one foot slightly ahead of the other so its heel is beside the other foot's big toe. Maintain your balance with your weight shared between both feet, then return to a wider stance without locking your knees.

name: Tandem Balance
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support with one foot directly in front of the other, heel near toe. Maintain an upright posture with your knees relaxed and your gaze forward, then return to a wider stance using the support as needed.

name: Single-Leg Balance
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support and shift your weight onto one foot. Lift the other foot slightly and maintain your balance while keeping your pelvis level, then place it down with control and use the support as needed.

name: Foam Surface Balance
desc: Place a firm balance pad on a nonslip floor beside a sturdy support and stand on it with your feet comfortably apart. Maintain an upright position while looking forward and breathing normally, using the support to step on and off safely.

name: Standing Balance with Eyes Closed
desc: Stand on a firm, level surface beside a sturdy support with your feet comfortably apart. Close your eyes only after finding a steady position, keep a hand near the support, and reopen your eyes before stepping or changing position.

name: Lateral Weight Shift
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support with your feet comfortably apart. Shift your weight slowly toward one foot and then the other while keeping both feet on the floor, your trunk upright, and your knees relaxed.

name: Forward and Backward Weight Shift
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support with your feet hip-width apart. Shift your body gently toward the balls of your feet and then toward your heels without lifting either part of the feet or bending at your waist.

name: Tandem Walking
desc: Stand beside a railing or counter with a clear path ahead. Walk forward by placing one heel near the toes of the opposite foot, keeping your gaze ahead and using the support as needed rather than crossing your feet.

name: Single-Leg Clock Reach
desc: Stand on one leg beside a sturdy support with the other foot lifted. Reach the free foot lightly forward, sideways, and backward as if toward points on a clock, returning it near the standing foot while keeping your pelvis level.

name: Standing March in Place
desc: Stand upright beside a sturdy support with your feet hip-width apart. Lift one knee and lower the foot, alternating sides while staying in place and keeping your trunk from leaning or your pelvis from dropping.

name: Alternating Step Taps
desc: Stand facing a low, stable step with a railing or sturdy support within reach. Touch one foot lightly onto the step and return it to the floor, alternating sides without pushing up onto the step or leaning backward.

name: Standing Multidirectional Reach
desc: Stand with your feet comfortably apart beside a sturdy support and place light targets within easy reach. Reach toward targets in front and to either side, returning upright between reaches while keeping both feet planted and avoiding a forced lean.

name: Unsupported Sitting Balance
desc: Sit near the front of a sturdy chair with your feet flat and your hands resting loosely in your lap. Maintain an upright position without leaning against the backrest, gently turning your head side to side while keeping your trunk steady.

name: Wobble Board Controlled Tilts
desc: Stand with both feet on a wobble board beside a secure railing, using your hands for support. Slowly tip the board's edges toward the floor in different directions and return toward level while keeping your knees soft and your trunk upright.

name: Standing Balance with Ball Toss
desc: Stand on a firm, level surface with your feet comfortably apart and a sturdy support beside you. Gently toss a soft ball between your hands at chest height, keeping your trunk upright and avoiding reaching after a ball that moves beyond your balance.

name: Clock Stepping
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support with your feet under your hips. Step one foot toward an imaginary clock point in front, to the side, or behind and transfer some weight onto it, then return to center while keeping your knees aligned with your feet.

name: Grapevine Cross-Stepping
desc: Stand beside a railing or counter with a clear sideways path. Step one foot across in front of the other, move the other foot sideways to uncross, and continue slowly while keeping your gaze forward and using the support as needed.

name: Sit-to-Stand
desc: Sit near the front of a sturdy chair with your feet flat and slightly behind your knees. Lean your trunk forward from your hips and push through your feet to stand, then lower back to the chair with control while keeping your knees aligned over your feet.

name: Seated Lateral Scooting
desc: Sit on a firm bench or sturdy chair with enough seat space to move sideways and both feet supported. Lean forward slightly, press through your feet and hands to lighten your hips, and shift sideways before settling fully onto the seat.

name: Chair Press-Up
desc: Sit in a sturdy chair with fixed armrests and your feet flat on the floor. Press down through the armrests to straighten your elbows and lift your hips slightly, then lower slowly while keeping your shoulders away from your ears.

name: Bed Rolling
desc: Lie on your back on a bed or mat with your knees bent. Reach one arm across your body and let your knees move toward the same side to roll onto your side, keeping your shoulders and pelvis moving together rather than twisting forcefully.

name: Supine-to-Sit Transfer
desc: Lie on your back near the side of a firm bed and roll onto your side. Lower your legs over the edge as you push through your upper hand and lower forearm to sit upright, pausing to find your balance with your feet supported.

name: Floor-to-Stand Transfer
desc: Start seated on a padded floor beside a stable chair or bench. Turn onto your hands and knees, bring one foot forward into a half-kneeling position, and use the support and front leg to rise while keeping the support firmly in place.

name: Tall-Kneeling Heel Sit
desc: Kneel upright on a padded surface with a sturdy support in front of you. Move your hips gently toward your heels and return to upright kneeling through your hips, keeping your trunk long and avoiding a forced bend at your knees.

name: Forward Walking with Heel-to-Toe Pattern
desc: Stand at the start of a clear, level path with your usual walking aid if one is used. Walk forward by placing the heel down first and rolling through the foot toward the toes, keeping your steps comfortable and your trunk upright.

name: Backward Walking
desc: Stand beside a railing or counter with a clear path behind you. Take small backward steps, placing the front of each foot down before the heel, while keeping your trunk upright and using the support as needed.

name: Sideways Walking
desc: Stand beside a railing or counter with your feet facing forward and your knees relaxed. Step sideways with one foot and bring the other toward it without crossing, keeping your pelvis level and using the support as needed.

name: Heel Walking
desc: Stand beside a railing or counter with a clear path ahead. Lift the fronts of your feet and take small forward steps on your heels while keeping your trunk upright and using the support as needed.

name: Toe Walking
desc: Stand beside a railing or counter with a clear path ahead. Rise onto the balls of your feet and take small forward steps while keeping your ankles upright and using the support as needed.

name: High-Knee Stepping Gait
desc: Stand beside a railing or counter with a clear path ahead. Walk forward while lifting each knee enough to clear the foot comfortably, placing it down with control and avoiding a backward lean or exaggerated back arch.

name: Obstacle Step-Over
desc: Place a low, soft obstacle on a clear, nonslip floor beside a railing or counter. Step over it with one foot and bring the other through, keeping your gaze ahead after locating the obstacle and using the support as needed.

name: Stair Ascent and Descent Practice
desc: Stand at the bottom of a staircase with a secure railing and no loose items on the steps. Climb and descend at a controlled pace with each foot securely placed, using the railing and bringing both feet to a step before continuing if needed.

name: Stepping Turns
desc: Stand beside a sturdy support on a clear, level surface. Change direction using several small steps, moving your feet with your body and avoiding twisting on a planted foot, then regain a steady stance.

name: Figure-Eight Walking
desc: Place two visible markers on a clear, level floor with enough space to walk around them. Walk in a figure-eight pattern using small steps through each turn, keeping your gaze along the path and your usual walking aid available if used.

name: Walking with Head Turns
desc: Stand beside a railing or counter with a clear path ahead. Walk slowly while gently turning your head to look left and right, returning your gaze forward between turns and using the support if your path becomes unsteady.

name: Walking Speed Changes
desc: Stand at the start of a clear, level path with your usual walking aid if one is used. Alternate between a comfortable pace and a slightly slower pace, changing gradually while keeping your steps controlled and your trunk upright.

name: Floor-to-Waist Lift
desc: Stand close to a light object on the floor with your feet comfortably apart. Bend through your hips and knees to grasp it, then straighten to bring it to waist height while keeping it close to your body and moving your feet to turn.

name: Shelf Reach and Place
desc: Stand close to a shelf at a comfortable height with a light object held near your body. Reach to place the object on the shelf and bring your arm back down, keeping your feet planted and avoiding a backward lean or forced overhead reach.

name: Walking While Carrying an Object
desc: Stand on a clear, level path holding a light object close to your body with both hands. Walk at a comfortable pace while looking ahead, keeping your shoulders relaxed and ensuring the object does not block your view of the path.

name: Stationary Cycling
desc: Sit on a stationary bicycle with the seat positioned so your knee remains slightly bent at the farthest pedal position. Pedal smoothly at a comfortable resistance while keeping your hips steady, your shoulders relaxed, and your knees aligned with your feet.

name: Recumbent Stepper
desc: Sit in a recumbent stepper with your back supported and your feet secured on the pedals according to the machine's instructions. Alternate pushing the pedals at a comfortable resistance, using the handles if provided while avoiding locking your knees or lifting your pelvis.

name: Upper Body Ergometer
desc: Sit or stand at an arm-cycle machine with its handles positioned for comfortable reach and a slight bend in your elbows. Turn the handles smoothly at a comfortable resistance while keeping your shoulders relaxed and avoiding rocking your trunk.

name: Elliptical Trainer
desc: Step onto an elliptical trainer using the fixed handrails and place both feet securely on the pedals. Move the pedals smoothly at a comfortable resistance while keeping your trunk upright and using the handrails for steady support.

name: Treadmill Walking
desc: Step onto a stopped treadmill, attach its safety clip, and position yourself near the handrails. Begin at a comfortable walking speed and walk with controlled steps, slowing and stopping the belt before stepping off.

name: Seated Marching
desc: Sit upright in a sturdy chair with your feet flat on the floor. Lift one knee and lower the foot, alternating sides at a comfortable pace while keeping your trunk steady and avoiding leaning backward.

name: Seated Alternating Punches
desc: Sit upright in a sturdy chair with your feet flat and your hands held loosely near your chest. Reach one hand forward and bring it back, alternating arms smoothly while keeping your shoulders relaxed and avoiding locking your elbows.

name: Low-Impact Step Jack
desc: Stand with your feet together and your arms relaxed at your sides beside a sturdy support. Step one foot sideways as your arms open outward within a comfortable range, then return and alternate sides without jumping or leaning backward.

name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
desc: Lie on your back with your knees supported or sit comfortably with one hand on your upper chest and the other on your abdomen. Breathe in gently through your nose so your abdomen rises, then breathe out easily while keeping your shoulders relaxed and avoiding an exaggerated breath.

name: Pursed-Lip Breathing
desc: Sit upright with your shoulders relaxed and your feet supported. Breathe in gently through your nose, then breathe out slowly through loosely pursed lips as if cooling a warm drink, avoiding forceful blowing or holding your breath.
